text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

<final_document>
**Subject: An apology about last season, and what we've changed**

Hi [Name],

You didn't renew your share this year, and I suspect last summer had something to do with it.

On July 9, a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next six weeks, your boxes had about half what they should have. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent just one short email about it. You paid for a full share and didn't get one, and you deserved a clearer explanation than I gave you. I'm sorry.

Here's what's different this year:

- **A second field on higher ground**, so not all our crops are in one place.
- **Two hail nets** over our tomatoes and peppers.
- **Pause credit:** you can now pause up to two weeks and get credit for them.

Those changes cost us $31,000, but a full share is still $540, the same as last year.

Sign-up closes March 15, and there are 52 shares left. We'd love to have you back on Thursdays.

[Sign-up link]

Thank you,
[Your name]
[Farm name]
</final_document>

The email is about 175 words. I didn't say the new field protects against hail, because you didn't tell me it does. I only said it spreads your crops across two places. If it was chosen for a specific reason, like better drainage or less exposure to storms, adding that in one short phrase would make the point stronger.
